text:
maria_support: Customer ticket #12345 - multiple clients getting 500s from /v1/generate for hosted API. Customer says it started ~15:55 UTC and they expect 429s for throttling not server errors. Sharing curl they used: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'`

jack_eng: seeing the same in our SLO graphs — big spike in 5xx from edge->quota path around 15:50-16:10. Traces show requests routed to quota-orch timed out and returned 500 instead of being classified as 429. Related logs:```
2026-03-17T15:52:03.312Z quota-orch v2 GET /check 00-abc - latency=60012ms -> TIMEOUT
2026-03-17T15:52:03.313Z rateguard edge -> quota-orch v2 error: upstream_timeout -> classify=500
```

sam_sre: alert fired on quota-orch latency (p95 > 30s). I just checked pods in us-west-2: several quota-orch v2 instances in CrashLoopBackOff and the fallback route wasn't configured; looks like routing policy had a deadlink to the fallback pool. Starting remediation: scaling down to force restart and enabling fallback route.

ops-bot: runbook step executed by sam_sre: `route set --edge rateguard --fallback quota-orch-legacy` 

jack_eng: quick mitigation helped—error rate dropped back to normal after switching fallback at 16:04 UTC. Confirming: after fallback, rateguard classifies overloaded responses as 429 and we see reduced 5xx.

kevin_prod: customer impact note: ACME corp lost ~12k requests in that 15m window, some payment webhook retries were affected. CS pinged and I'm scheduling an incident postmortem with them.

linda_cs: I've replied to customer with acknowledgement and ETA. They asked for root cause and timeline; will include mitigation steps and follow-up on ensuring 429s are returned when quota is exceeded.

jack_eng: preliminary root cause: quota-orch v2 had an internal connection pool leak under a burst pattern from a partner tenant; without healthy fallback route configured, rateguard attempted the v2 route and timed out waiting for quota-orch -> surfaced as 5xx. Fixes: 1) hotfix rollback v2 -> v1 for quota-orch in us-west-2, 2) add circuit-breaker + lower upstream timeout on rateguard, 3) add alert that monitors classification ratio (5xx vs 4xx) on edge->quota path.

maria_support: repro steps for engineering:
1) run the repro loop used by customer: `for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done`
2) tail rateguard logs for `classify=500` and check upstream latency to quota-orch
3) reproduce with client rate ~200 rps to see pool exhaustion behavior

jack_eng: added a short-lived hotfix: lowered rateguard upstream timeout from 60s -> 5s to fail-fast and return 429 when quota-orch slow. This reduces customer-visible 500s while we fix the leak. Will revert after we deploy circuit breakers.

sam_sre: follow-ups: rolling restart of quota-orch v2 in us-west-2, deploy pool-leak fix (PR #3482), add alert and update runbook. Scheduling postmortem meeting 16:30 UTC tomorrow.

maria_support: marking this as sev-2 for customer impact, will update ticket and coordinate postmortem notes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
